Buying an eighth of the size at a fifth more a unit is the ladder working as quoted, not a concession lost. WHAT IT MOVES IS THE FLOOR, NOT THE LEDGER. Replacement cost is read off the newest received lot, so from this row every floor on the desk is built on RM56 instead of RM47, roughly a fifth higher, and the pending rows should be re-read against it rather than against the figures written beside them last week. ASSUMPTION, STATED: the entry was queued as completed with the full RM700 in cash and 12.5 unit moved, so it is taken as paid and received in full on the 13th.

The order went paid, then refunded, then paid and collected, all inside two days: RM400 on 28 Jul against nothing delivered, the RM400 returned on 29 Jul which reverted it to pending, and then on 29 Jul he came back, paid again and took the salt. Net of the three steps it is RM400 in and 5 unit out, so it is now COMPLETED and counts everywhere. The trail is kept in all three steps rather than tidied to a single payment, because the refund is the only record that the desk once wrote a price under its own floor and nearly lost the sale over it. He arrived on a provisional code and was named on 29 Jul, so the desk re-keyed him to CE4-AD and purged the placeholder. The price is the thing to keep in view: RM80/unit sat UNDER the floor, since the board quotes RM470 for this size and will not go below RM415, so RM400 was RM15 light. It earns RM33/unit against the RM47 lot it came off, but only RM17.86/unit against the RM62.14 it costs to replace.

GOODWILL, not a sale and not a correction. The reconciliation stands at 4.1912 unit and he was owed exactly that; this 0.5588 unit is given on top, taking him to the 4.75 unit he had asked for, because he is among the most loyal names on the book. It is booked IN-KIND at cost, RM26.26, not at his RM68 selling rate. Recording it matters because salt that leaves the shelf with no line against it books as shrinkage, and a deliberate gift is not a loss. Valuing it at COST matters just as much: at the selling rate it would have carried RM11.74 of margin, so a giveaway would have IMPROVED gross margin, which is plainly wrong. At cost the revenue and the expense are the same figure and margin is untouched; what the gift actually costs shows where it should, in the salt no longer on the shelf. Stated plainly for the record: the desk was not shown to be wrong. The 25 Jul offset of 2.0588 unit was agreed and is evidenced in the trail; conceding the difference is a commercial choice about a relationship, not an accounting correction, and the next reconciliation starts from the ledger rather than from this.

His second order, agreed 31 Jul: 0.5 unit at RM80. Nothing paid and nothing delivered, so it is PENDING and counts nowhere. RM160/unit is the retired M card exactly for this size, so it is a card price rather than a concession below the ladder. It is still worth looking at twice: his first order paid RM210/unit, the best rate this desk has ever achieved and the reference the lot outlook uses as its ceiling at this size. Agreeing RM160 with the one buyer who proved RM210 gives away RM25 on a half unit, on the most profitable size the desk sells. He may simply not pay RM210 again; that is worth finding out before it becomes his standing rate.

A reward is not a gift of nothing; it is a price the desk chose to settle another way, and every other rebate row on this book already carries one. Where a redemption has no price basis of its own, TIER I is the basis, per his instruction on 07 Aug.

sales.note: His second order, agreed for Monday 03 Aug. It was RECORDED as 5 unit at RM440 and that was a clerical error: the order was always 2 unit at RM185. It did NOT stay pending: both units went out on 04 Aug and the RM90 landed on 05 Aug, so the order is delivered and settled and both the money and the quantity count. THE TRAIL ON SCREEN IS SHORT BY THREE STEPS. This row carries two amend keys and JavaScript keeps only the last, so the three Fulfilment steps are discarded and the clerical Modification alone survives, which is why the Order book still reads the order as open. NO FIGURE MOVES: the stated deliveredOn, paidOn and cash carry the movements, and txPaid reads the full RM180. The merge is HELD FOR INSTRUCTION rather than done quietly, because the discarded trail values the redeemed unit at RM95 and the row values it at RM90, a RM5 difference that is his call and not the desk’s. RM92.50/unit is exactly the rate of his first order, so this is his established price rather than the RM88 the mis-recorded larger lot implied. The price is RM90/unit, which is RM180 over 2 unit and exactly the good price on today’s ladder. The RM88, the floor and the RM460 card in the sentence this replaces were all figures from the 5 unit order that never existed. His first order paid RM92.50/unit, so he has moved down the curve RM4.50 a unit while more than doubling the size, which is roughly how a ladder is supposed to be used. The desk booked it twice wrongly before this: first as a part-fulfilment of a 5 unit order, then as a completed 2 unit sale. Both came from the same input fault, since the Modification fields were labelled Cash moved and Salt moved, so a corrected QUANTITY and TOTAL were read as money and salt changing hands. Fixed at v177; this row is the correction against the 15 unit reorder trigger.

CN6-WM’s FIRST sale as an associate, appointed the same day. The end buyer is a stranger, so it books to his GENERAL BUCKET, CN6-WM-R, and not to a code of his own: a named downstream is earned only where you delivered to the person yourself and so know who he is. The queue asked for a named code, CN6-WM-1-TBC, and that was wrong at source: the location read TBC, which is an admission that the place was not known, and a place is exactly what earns a code under the split rule. Corrected at v201 and the named code PURGED outright rather than kept as an alias, per the standing one-identifier rule. It was queued as a DIRECT sale and is booked as an R2 downsell, so the counterparty is CN6-WM and the bucket is the downstream. Both corrections point the same way: assocOf() resolves a -Gen code back to its reseller, so the credit now reaches him by construction rather than by my having noticed. Paid and collected on the day, so it folds into the opening line and carries no amendment trail. THE PRICE IS THE THING TO LOOK AT. 6.5 unit for RM440 is RM67.69/unit. It breaches nothing: the floor is RM417.48 and the floor RM420, so it clears them by RM22.52 and RM20. But it clears them only because 6.5 unit is a QUARTER OF A UNIT over the 6.25 retail boundary, and that quarter-unit drops the floor from 25% to 2%. The last carded size below it, 6.25 unit, quotes RM540 on the retired R card against a RM524.53 floor. So a customer taking 0.25 unit MORE salt paid RM100 LESS money, and the ladder permitted it. It is RM125 under the engine’s own RM565 quote and earns 7.0% on the RM62.94 effective cost, RM20.69/unit over the RM47 lot for RM134.50 gross. This is plan P11’s argument in a single order, and it is the first one on the book to cross that boundary since the cap was proposed.

Direct repeat, and an exact one: 2 unit for RM220 is the SAME size at the SAME price as his 23 Jul order, RM110/unit. RM220 at 2 unit IS the retired R card, to the ringgit, against a RM152.33 floor and a the floor, so it clears both with RM67.67 to spare and needed no negotiation to get there. Paid and collected on the day it was agreed, so the settlement folds into the opening line and the row carries no amendment trail. Drawn from the RM47 lot, so RM126/unit on lot cost and a margin over replacement that the desk computes live, because a figure typed here goes stale the moment the buying rate moves. Booked DIRECT, deliberately, and the attribution still reaches CS6-BS. He is a named buyer under that reseller, but both earlier orders to him, 23 Jul and 30 Jul, were booked direct with no assoc field, and this follows them rather than inventing a third treatment. The credit is not lost by doing so: assocOf() finds the 15 Jul R2 row that carries him as its downstream and resolves the owner from there, so the Network tab reads him under CS6-BS by construction. That is the standing trap with named associate codes, and it does not bite here because the earlier row already anchors him.

RE-BOOKED 07 Aug: this was written as CS6-PER buying for himself and it is an R2 RESELL, so it belongs to CS6-PER-R with his 07 Aug one. RM80 a unit. It moves RM240 out of his own buying and into his R2 turnover, which now stands at RM400 against a RM500 rebate step, so he is RM100 of resell away from a free unit rather than RM340.

His second resell as an associate. The end buyer is a stranger, so it books to his GENERAL BUCKET, CN6-WM-R, with CN6-WM-R as the counterparty, exactly as his 03 Aug downsell and the CS6-BS ones do. The bucket is not a customer and is never issued a statement. Paid and collected on the day, so it folds into the opening line and carries no amendment trail. THE RATE IS THE BEST THIS DESK HAS EVER TAKEN ON A RESELL, AND IT IS NOT CLOSE. RM250 for 2 unit is RM125/unit to the desk, against RM67.69/unit on his own 6.5 unit resell three days ago: the same reseller, the same bucket, nearly double the rate. It is also RM15/unit ABOVE the retired R card, which quotes RM220 at 2 unit, and RM95 above the floor. A reseller paying over the retail card has to clear more than retail downstream to earn anything, which is worth understanding before it is treated as the new normal: either he is selling into a pocket that bears more than this book has tested, or the 03 Aug rate was the anomaly and this is the correction. Drawn from the RM47 lot, so RM78/unit on lot cost for RM156 gross, and a margin over replacement that the desk computes live, because a figure typed here goes stale the moment the buying rate moves. IT ALSO EARNS HIM A FREE UNIT. His R2 turnover goes from RM440 to RM690 and crosses the RM500 rebate step, so a second free unit is earned against one already redeemed. Nothing is handed over here: he has no advance outstanding for it to offset, so it stands as owed until he asks, exactly as the first one did.

Redeems the free unit earned when his R2 turnover crossed RM500 on the RM250 resell. No advance outstanding to offset, so it goes out as salt. Valued at the Tier I ask of RM80 for a unit and settled in kind, per his rule of 07 Aug that a redemption with no price basis of its own uses Tier I. It carried RM0 until v263, which is the same fault as his 04 Aug half unit: 1 unit off the shelf at RM47 against nothing at all, so the ledger read a 100% loss on a reward he had earned. Earned 2, applied 2, nothing owed either way.

THE FIRST OIL SALE ON THE BOOK. A resell through CS6-BS to an end buyer with no name, so it books to his general bucket exactly as a salt downsell does, with CS6-BS-R as the counterparty. Paid and delivered on the day, nothing owed. THE QUANTITY IS 10 UNIT, NOT 1, AND THE COST IS RM7, NOT RM100. Oil is measured in tens: corrected at v229, after v226 recorded the ladder as a selling card and v228 corrected that half of it while leaving the basis of measurement a tenth of what it should be. On the right numbers this sold at RM13/unit against a RM7 lot, so RM60 on RM130, a 46.2% margin, against the 23.1% the desk reported an hour ago and the ‘unknown’ it reported before that. Three readings of one row, and only this one is the trade that happened. COSTED FIFO ACROSS TWO LOTS at v230, once the opening rate was known. The shelf held 5 unit of opening oil, off a 30 unit lot at RM230, so RM7.667/unit; the 50 unit lot landed the same day at RM7. Oldest goes first, so this order took the 5 opening unit and 5 new ones: RM73.33 of cost, RM56.67 of margin, 43.6%. Not the RM60 at 46.2% the desk showed at v229, when the opening rate was unknown and the whole order was costed at the new lot. RM3.33 is a small number and the discipline is not: costing a sale at the cheapest lot on the shelf flatters every margin it touches. It is also worth seeing the spread in one row: RM13/unit is where he sells, RM10/unit is the dearest tier SP7-PUD quotes, and RM7 to RM7.667 is what the oil actually cost.
Agreed 06 Aug, paid and collected on the 8th. It sat deferred for a few hours between the payment and the handover and closed the same day, so it draws as one line.
Agreed 06 Aug at the Tier II ask of RM90, settled in full the next day. Marked from the ledger card and committed at v256.

Quoted at RM300 on the 7th and REQUOTED at RM260 before anything moved, then paid and delivered in full on the 8th. It is restated rather than amended: a price re-agreed before any cash or salt moves is the price, not a movement, so the row carries the final terms and the history sits here. RM86.67 a unit, which is the TIER II ask at 3 unit given to a customer whose single order puts him in Tier III at RM300. A RM40 concession to open the account, RM49 clear of the RM211 floor and RM26.67 a unit of margin above replacement.

His SECOND resell, and the first was re-booked to this same account on the day this one was written, which is why the note beneath it says his turnover starts here when it does not. Priced at RM80 a unit, the same rate as his 05 Aug resell, which is what he asked for. It clears the RM143 floor at 2 unit by RM17 and sits RM60 under the Tier III card, so the margin on this resell is thinner than on anything he buys for himself. It also starts his R2 turnover at RM160, RM340 short of the first rebate step.

Oil, not salt, and the desk now prices it on its own ladder. RM100 for 10 unit is exactly Tier I on the oil board, RM10 a unit. A RESELL like his salt, so it books to CS6-PER-R. It is the balance of a RM260 order taken with his 2 unit salt resell: RM160 of salt and RM100 of oil. Only the second oil order this book has ever written and the first to a party who also buys salt.

HALF PAID, HALF REDEEMED. 2 unit at RM160: RM80 STILL TO COME and RM80 settled by the free unit he was awarded today, valued at the Tier I ask of RM80 for a unit. It books to his OWN code rather than CS6-PER-R because the reward is his, not his resell account’s, and rebateApplied reads the plain code; it is the same shape as CI4-OKR’s 03 Aug order, where rebateKg names how many units of reward the row consumed. No separate salt movement for the free unit: 2 unit leave the shelf and 1 unit of reward is drawn down against them. Earned 1, applied 1, nothing owed either way. CORRECTED TWICE ON 08 Aug, and both were my assumption rather than his instruction. First the cash half was booked as received and it is not; he will pay it. Then the salt was booked as handed over and it has NOT been: he stated a price and a settlement and said nothing about delivery, and I filled the gap. Nothing has moved. The reward is drawn down and RM80 of value is settled, so the desk OWES him salt: the order reads Open, paid ahead of delivery, and there is no receivable because you cannot be owed money for goods you have not handed over. The rate is RM80 a unit against the Tier II board of RM180 at 2 unit, but half of it was never going to be cash.

RM100 for a unit, Tier II where his single order puts him in Tier III at RM120: a RM20 concession he did not ask for, stated by him. Paid and collected on the 8th. It is his SECOND order, so he leaves Tier III with it: from the next quote he is Tier II by the ledger rather than by concession.

PENDING, and PLANNED FOR 07 AUG rather than agreed on it: the date is the intention, not a movement. Nothing paid and nothing delivered, so it counts nowhere and the 12.5 unit stays free to sell until it moves. An exact repeat of his 15 Jul order, same 12.5 unit, same RM850, same RM68/unit. AND IT IS NO LONGER THE PROBLEM IT WAS. This note said for days that RM850 sat RM102 UNDER FLOOR against a floor of RM952.06, then that it cleared a RM824.95 floor by RM25.05. BOTH ARE STALE, AND IT IS BACK UNDER. The 12 Aug hand count of 1.30 took the leak from 17.18% to 20.28%, the CR3-PUD unit gave 0.42% of that back, and the floor at 12.5 unit now stands at RM852.40, so RM850 is RM2.40 SHORT of it. Read live off floorTotal(12.5) on 13 Aug, not computed by hand. The figure has now crossed the order twice in a fortnight without a single thing changing in the order itself, which is the whole argument for never printing a floor. The order never got worse; the cost base moved twice under it, first against it and then back. The leak now stands at 17.18% after four units were traced to the founding member on 10 Aug, and the cost is unlocked, so this figure follows the book rather than a snapshot. What it still does: at RM68/unit against the RM47 lot actually on the shelf it makes RM21/unit, RM262.50 on the lot, so it is cash-positive and comfortably above what the salt cost. What it does now do: cover the RM56.99 a unit it costs to REPLACE that salt, plus the 15% markup the single floor asks. There is no wholesale band any more, and no separate floor. Left visible rather than suppressed, and left pending rather than repriced. He is the second largest customer on the book at RM1,566 and this lot is 31% of the free shelf, so it is a real decision and not an arithmetic one: hold the relationship at RM850, or take it to RM955 and find out. Nothing is booked either way until it moves.

amend.note: 1 unit handed over at RM90 with nothing paid
RM90 paid in full on the 11th, three days out and inside terms. Queued from the phone and committed here.

sales.note: ADVANCE, NOW SETTLED. The unit went out on the 8th and the money did not; RM90 landed on the 11th, three days later, and the order completes. It was the only receivable on the book while it stood and it also held him exactly at the 1 unit retail credit cap, so both readings clear with it: the cap is free again and the sole open advance is now CR3-DAM’s. Worth noting against his own words: he told the desk on 06 Aug he is reducing his salt intake and to expect smaller, less frequent orders, and this is the same 1 unit at the same RM90 he took on the 6th, so the size is consistent with what he said and the account is now square. It books to SALT, which is what the entry said: the Transaction tab could not name a product until v275, so this is the last row on the book whose product was implied rather than chosen.
Half a unit at RM100/unit, paid and collected on the day. His SIXTH order at exactly RM100/unit, which makes it the steadiest rate on the book rather than a quote. Drawn from the RM47 lot.

amend.note: 1 unit handed over at RM80 with nothing paid
the RM80 lands on Wednesday 12 Aug, the day it was promised for, four days out and inside his term. Reported on the 13th, which is why the desk was still calling it past due.

sales.note: ADVANCE, SETTLED ON THE DAY IT WAS PROMISED. 1 unit handed over at RM80 on the 8th with nothing paid, and the RM80 paid on Wednesday 12 Aug, four days out. THE DESK WAS WRONG ABOUT HIM, AND THE RECORD SHOULD SAY SO. Until this entry the row read PAST DUE and named him the only receivable on the book, on the reasoning that the promised Wednesday had passed with no money. The money had in fact arrived on that Wednesday; what had not arrived was the report of it, on the 13th. A promise kept looked identical to a promise broken because the desk only ever sees what is queued, and the gap between a movement and its recording is the one thing it cannot observe. With this the book carries NO receivable and NO open advance at all, CC5-OKR’s RM90 having cleared on the 11th, and his 1 unit retail credit cap is free again rather than sitting at the line.

His LARGEST order, 4 unit at RM90/unit, paid and collected on the day. The rate is cut from his standing RM110 as the reward for taking his cumulative buying past RM1,000: RM650 before this order, RM1,010 with it. Booked DIRECT and NOT tagged to his associate, because only a referred customer’s FIRST order carries the introduction.

THE FOUNDING MEMBER’S FOUR EARNED UNITS, RECORDED AT LAST. He earned four against RM2,090 of referrals and he took them, but the salt left the shelf with no row against it and was absorbed by the shrinkage plug, where it read as loss rather than as a reward that was genuinely earned. Booking it moves 4 unit OUT of the unexplained plug, which falls from 44.56 to 40.56, and the leak with it. THE DATE IS THE RECORDING DATE, NOT THE MOVEMENT DATE, which is not known; correct it and the FIFO lot follows, though every lot since 28 Jul is RM47 so the cost does not move. Valued at cost and settled in kind, so no revenue arises. He has since DEPARTED, so he comes off the bench while his history stays.

SETTLED, AND NOW DATED. It was agreed on 11 Aug with nothing paid and nothing handed over, which is why it stood undated and counted nowhere; the money and the salt both moved on the 12th, queued from the phone and committed here. So it dates from the agreement on the 11th and its movements are stamped on the 12th, the same shape as CC5-OKR’s advance. 2.5 unit for RM230 is RM92 a unit, the same terms he took on 23 Jul and 31 Jul, and his 06 Aug order held the same RM230 while the size went to 3, so RM92 a unit is his standing price rather than a quote. Drawn from the RM47 lot, so RM45 a unit and RM112.50 on the order at 48.9%. The 2.5 unit now come off the shelf, which they had not while the row was pending. The wording it replaces, kept because the rule is the point: PENDING, and therefore carrying NO DATE. Agreed on 11 Aug with nothing paid and nothing handed over, and an agreed-on date is an intention rather than a movement, so the row is undated and counts nowhere: no revenue, no cost of goods, no stock drawn, and the 2.5 unit stay free to sell until they move. His FOURTH order at exactly this size and price: 2.5 unit for RM230, RM92 a unit, the same terms he took on 23 Jul and on 31 Jul, and his 06 Aug order held the same RM230 while the size went to 3. Four orders inside three weeks at one rate makes RM92 a unit his standing price rather than a quote, which is why this needed no negotiation. It clears its floor for the size, and the desk computes that floor live from cost rather than reading a figure typed here.

THE LARGEST OIL ORDER ON THE BOOK, and the first bought DIRECT rather than resold. 30 unit for RM330 is RM11 a unit, paid and collected on the day, nothing owed. Every oil order before this one went through a reselling account: his own 06 Aug downsell of 10 unit and CS6-PER-R’s 10 unit on the 7th. This is the associate buying for himself, which puts it on the CUSTOMER hurdle rather than the associate one. On a RM7 lot it makes RM4 a unit, RM120 on the order at 36.4%, the best absolute margin any oil order has returned. The rate sits between the RM13 a unit his own downsell fetched on the 6th and the RM10 top of SP7-PUD’s quoted ladder, so buying three times the size at RM11 is a volume rate rather than a concession.

THE FIRST ORDER THIS BOOK HAS EVER SOLD BELOW COST. 20 unit for RM120 is RM6 a unit against a RM7 lot, so it loses RM20 on RM120 of revenue, a margin of minus 16.7%. Nothing about the entry is ambiguous: it was queued as paid, delivered and completed, and it is booked as it was queued. It is an R2 resell through CS6-BS to an end buyer with no name and no location, so it books to his general bucket, CS6-BS-R, with that bucket as the counterparty, exactly as his salt downsells do; the bucket is not a customer and is never issued a statement. The queue wrote it against a CS6-BS-Gen bucket, which was absorbed into CS6-BS-R at v280, so it is re-keyed here rather than minting a retired code. THE RATE IS THE THING TO LOOK AT. RM6 a unit is less than half the RM13 the same reseller fetched on 06 Aug and RM1 under the sharpest rate SP7-PUD has ever quoted the desk, so it cannot be explained by supply. Either it was priced off the wrong ladder or it was a clearance decision taken deliberately; the desk cannot tell which from the entry, and it earns nothing under the reward scheme either way, because a margin under 30% sits in the bottom band.

A NEW CUSTOMER, OPENED AT CY2-NIL. 2 unit for RM230 is RM115 a unit, paid and delivered on the day with nothing owed. It is a strong opening rate: above CA4-DAM’s RM100 anchor and CE4-CHE’s RM92 standing price, and just under the RM116.67 a unit CA4-DAM paid on 26 Jul, so a first order took a full rate and no introductory discount was given. On the RM47 lot it returns RM68 a unit, RM136 on the order at 59.1%, which is the best margin any retail order has returned. He is added to the roster as an ordinary retail customer, not an associate, so he carries the 1 unit credit cap; nothing is owed, so the cap is untouched. The name and the location are in the directory and never in this file.

Half a unit at RM100 a unit, paid and collected on the day. His SEVENTH order at exactly RM100 a unit, which makes it the steadiest rate on the book by some distance. Drawn from the RM47 lot, so RM26.50 on RM50 at 53%. THE DATE IS ASSUMED: the instruction gave no date and reported the order completed, so it is booked today, 12 Aug. Correct it and the FIFO lot follows, though every salt lot since 28 Jul is RM47 so the cost does not move.

A NEW CUSTOMER, OPENED AT CR3-PUD, AND CN6-WM BROUGHT HIM. 1 unit for RM110, paid and delivered on the day with nothing owed. The introduction is tagged R3 to CN6-WM in full, which is what a first order from a referred customer carries and what no later order of his will: the credit is for bringing him, not for his continued trade, and he buys on his own line from here. RM110 is a strong opening rate. It sits RM10 under the RM120 a T3 buyer with no history is asked and RM10 over the RM100 anchor, so an introductory concession was given and it was a small one; CY2-NIL opened at RM115 a unit the day before, so two new names in two days both took above-anchor rates. On the RM47 lot it returns RM63 a unit, RM63 on the order at 57.3%. He is an ordinary retail customer and not an associate, so he carries the 1 unit credit cap; nothing is owed, so the cap is untouched. THE DATE IS STATED: 12 AUG, AND IT SITS INSIDE THAT DAY’S COUNT. It was first booked on the 13th, the day it was reported, then moved to the 11th on his word that it preceded the count, then fixed at the 12th when he gave the day. SO THIS COUNT IS AN EXCEPTION TO THE START-OF-DATE RULE, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF SAYING SO. This desk reads a count as at the START of its date, which is why deliveries dated the same day normally come OFF it. Not here: the 1.30 was counted at the END of the 12th, after this unit had gone, and he has said so plainly. Anyone applying the usual rule to these two rows would take the unit off the shelf a second time and put the shelf at 0.30, which is exactly the mistake v296 made and v297 undid. THE SHELF DOES NOT MOVE AND THE PLUG DOES. The count already absorbed this unit, so 1.30 stands; what changes is that a unit the plug was carrying as unexplained loss is now explained as a sale, and the leak falls with it. The FIFO lot does not follow the date either way: every salt lot since 28 Jul is RM47. The name and the location are in the directory and never in this file.

AN ADVANCE, AND HIS FIFTH CONSECUTIVE ORDER AT EXACTLY RM80. 1 unit handed over on the 14th with nothing paid. RM80 on 15 Jul, 20 Jul, 30 Jul, 08 Aug and now, after RM85 on 29 Jun and RM90 on 03 Jul, so RM80 stopped being a quote some weeks ago and is his price. The shape is his last order repeated exactly, 1 unit at RM80 on credit, and that one was paid four days out on the Wednesday he promised. It is the only receivable on the book, CC5-OKR’s RM90 having cleared on the 11th, and it puts him back at his 1 unit retail credit cap, so nothing further goes out to him until this is paid. The desk should not read a delay as a broken promise this time either. The 08 Aug row spent four days marked past due when the money had in fact arrived on the day agreed and only the report of it was late; the gap the desk cannot see is between a movement and its queueing, not between a promise and its keeping. FIFO takes the unit off the 1.30 unit remnant at RM47, so RM33 on RM80 at 41.3%. It is the last unit on the book to be costed at RM47.

THE FIRST ROW ON THIS BOOK WHOSE COST IS A BLEND OF TWO LOTS. 1.5 unit for RM175 is RM116.67 a unit, paid and delivered on the day, CN6-WM’s third resell as an associate and an R2 through his general bucket, the end buyer being a stranger with no code of their own, exactly as his 03 Aug and 06 Aug downsells were booked. The cost is RM54.20 a unit and it is not a lot rate. The 1.30 unit remnant had 0.30 left after CR3-DAM took a unit that morning, so 0.30 comes off it at RM47 and the other 1.20 off the 13 Aug lot at RM56: RM81.30 on the order, RM54.20 a unit. Every row since 28 Jul has read a single RM47, which is why this one is worth pointing at. The 0.30 is carried at the RM47 the rows use rather than the RM47.47 STOCK_COST blends to; the difference is RM0.14 on the order and the honest caveat about where the plug fell already sits at STOCK_COST. On that basis it returns RM62.47 a unit, RM93.70 on the order at 53.5%. The rate is holding as the size falls. He resold 6.5 unit at RM67.69 on the 3rd, 2 unit at RM125 on the 6th and 1.5 at RM116.67 now, so the small-parcel rate has printed twice above RM115 and the RM67.69 looks like the outlier rather than the trend.

PENDING, and therefore carrying NO DATE: nothing paid, nothing delivered, so it counts nowhere, draws no stock and the unit stays free to sell until it moves. THE THING TO LOOK AT IS THE PRICE, WHICH IS RM10 UNDER HIS OWN STANDING RATE. He has paid RM90 a unit every time he has traded: the 09 Jul barter, the 15 Jul cash sale and the 08 Aug advance that settled on the 11th, with a fourth at RM90 cancelled on 20 Jul before anything moved. RM80 would be the first time he is asked for less, and nothing in the entry says why. It also lands on the wrong side of the restock. The 13 Aug lot puts replacement cost at RM56 rather than RM47, so the single-unit floor rises with it and RM80 needs reading against the floor the desk computes live, not against the RM47-era arithmetic on the rows above. He said on 06 Aug he was reducing his intake and to expect smaller, less frequent orders, and 1 unit is consistent with that; a smaller order at a cut rate is not. Left pending and left visible rather than repriced, because whether RM80 was a decision or a slip is his to say and the desk cannot tell from the entry.

A NEW CUSTOMER, OPENED AT CH4-MLR, AND THE FIRST NAME TAKEN STRAIGHT OFF THE DESK. 1 unit for RM110, paid and delivered on the day with nothing owed, and an oil unit alongside it on its own row. He came in with no associate behind him, so nothing is tagged and no introduction credit arises. RM110 IS THE SAME OPENING RATE CR3-PUD TOOK, AND IT IS NO LONGER THE SAME SALE. That one was written against a RM47 shelf and returned RM63 a unit at 57.3%; this one draws the 13 Aug RM56 lot, so the same RM110 returns RM54 a unit, RM54 on the order at 49.1%. Eight points of margin went to the restock and not to the customer, which is the clearest illustration on the book of why this desk refuses to print a floor. It still sits above the RM100 anchor and RM10 under the RM120 a T3 buyer with no history is asked, so a small introductory concession was given, the same one CR3-PUD got. He is an ordinary retail customer and not an associate, so he carries the 1 unit credit cap; nothing is owed, so the cap is untouched. ASSUMPTION, STATED: the date and the settlement. It was reported as a completed sale with no date given and no terms mentioned, so it is booked today, 14 Aug, as paid and delivered in full, the same reading the CA4-DAM row of 12 Aug took. Correct either and the FIFO lot follows. The name and the location are in the directory and never in this file.

RM11.50, CORRECTED FROM RM115 ON HIS WORD, AND THE CATCH IS THE POINT OF THE ROW. 1 unit for RM11.50, paid and delivered on the day, opening CH4-MLR on oil the same day he opened on salt. On the RM7 lot it returns RM4.50, 39.1% margin on the price, which is a 64.3% markup on cost and therefore sits between the good rung at 50% and the great one at 75%. The two figures are the same sale said two ways and this row states both on purpose: the ledger quotes margin on price, the v300 ladder is markup on cost, and reading 39.1% against a 25% floor would compare the wrong pair. THE RATE NOW READS CORRECTLY AGAINST EVERY OTHER OIL ROW. It lands between the RM11 CS6-BS paid buying 30 unit direct and the RM13 his downsell fetched, which is the right ordering: one unit should cost more per unit than thirty, and at RM115 it did not sit on the ladder at all. WHAT v300 DID WITH IT IS WORTH KEEPING. The figure came in at RM115 and was booked at RM115, because this desk records what it is told and does not quietly move a number into the range it expected; the same rule booked the RM6 below-cost resell of 11 Aug without argument. What it did instead was say plainly that RM115 was ten times any rate on the book, name RM11.50 as the one-digit alternative, and put a figure on being wrong: RM103.50 of overstated oil revenue and a 93.9% margin that never happened. He read it and corrected it inside a day. THAT IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT FOR DRAFTING A ROW AND HAVING IT APPROVED rather than committing a queued entry straight to the ledger: the entry looked ordinary, and it was the ROW, with its cost and its margin beside it, that showed the fault.

contacts.note: replied: reducing his salt intake, so expect smaller and less frequent orders rather than none

loans.note: Offset against the 6.5 unit deferred on the package sale. Went out on 12 May, six weeks BEFORE the 26 Jun opening count, so the 4.90 unit counted that day is already net of it.

supplierReceivable.note: Paid for 12.5 unit that never arrived. 12 Jul: he was found to have had an accident and an in-person meeting was requested. He has since gone unresponsive, so on 31 Jul, 23 days out and already 100% provisioned, the desk WROTE IT OFF. The provision stays charged; what changes is that the desk no longer counts it as expected cash. Any recovery is upside against a book that has already taken the hit.

customerRefunds.note: Overpaid: paid RM180 against his RM100 order (1 unit at RM100), so RM80 was owed back as a cash refund. Flagged in the 24 Jul delivery audit, PAID on 31 Jul: the liability clears and the RM80 leaves cash on that date. The entry stays rather than being deleted, because a refund that vanished would also delete the only record of the overpayment.

banned.soldAfter: 1 unit sold 30 Jul via amendment, paid in full
banned.note: Removed from the associate bench and barred from any further sale on 26 Jul. LIFTED FORMALLY on 30 Jul by his decision, after the RM290 was settled in full and one unit had already gone out via amendment at RM130, paid on the spot. The entry stays rather than being deleted, because four days of ban and the breach that ended it are facts about the book. He may buy again; the associate bench is a separate standing and this lift does not restore it.

departed.note: Departed the business for personal reasons. Memorialised as Co-Founder, a title held by him alone and not passed on. His RM2,090 of introductions and the five customers behind them stay attributed to him.

roles.title: Chief Business Development Officer
roles.note: Vacant. The work CJ4-OKR did in substance is now a named position rather than a personal arrangement, so it can be filled by someone else without inheriting his title.

CS6-PER.why: Oil turnover counted at his direction: RM400 of salt plus RM100 of oil is exactly the RM500 step.

RM48/unit; moved dearer (was RM2,200 at RM44/unit)

SOURCING_PLAN.label: end August
SOURCING_PLAN.basis: His own reading: a big monthly lot, and enough on the shelf that next week needs nothing.
SOURCING_PLAN.rateBasis: the 100 unit tier, the largest quoted and the rate actually paid on 28 Jul. There is no 150 unit tier: this is an assumption, not a quote.

CASH_COUNT_RETIRED.note: Counted by hand on 28 Jul. The opening balance on 26 Jun was never recorded, so it is derived from this count rather than guessed.

ONE_OFFS.note: Judged a rare one-off. Treat the RM104/unit it paid as an outlier, not as evidence of what wholesale will bear.
